title: MCP tool inspect_overworld_session_story advertises an empty schema
body:
`inspect_overworld_session_story` advertises `{"type":"object","properties":{}}` — no
properties, no required fields — while the server rejects any call that omits
`story_choice_id` ("Required at story_choice_id"). A client that builds calls from the
advertised schema cannot construct a valid one.

Verified independently of the reports: a `tools/list` against the server returns 43 tools,
and this is the ONLY one with an empty property set.

Cause: every other tool passes a raw Zod shape to the `tool()` helper, which the MCP SDK
converts to JSON Schema. This one passes a built schema instead —
`z.object({...}).refine(...)` — to express that `option_id` and `reveal_id` are mutually
exclusive. The SDK cannot read properties off the resulting effects wrapper, so it emits an
empty object. `tool()` accepts `ZodRawShape | z.ZodTypeAny | $ZodType`, so this type-checks
and fails silently at the schema boundary.

Note the same file already solves this problem correctly elsewhere: `requireArgumentGroups`
builds a `$ZodType` via `z4.pipe` for tools with cross-field requirements, and those tools
DO advertise full schemas. So the fix is to express the mutual exclusion the same way rather
than with a trailing `.refine()`, and the pattern to copy is a few lines up in the file.

Impact is above cosmetic. Two independent playtesters called this tool load-bearing: it is
the only route to a read-only reveal that defines the four quest plans (LURE / DRIVE /
FORTIFY / HUNT), which one lead identified as the fix for the opening's biggest
comprehension problem. A schema-validating client would strip the arguments and never reach
it.

Repro:
  1. Start the MCP server on stdio.
  2. initialize, then tools/list.
  3. Read the entry for inspect_overworld_session_story: properties is {}.

Suggested guard: a structural test asserting every registered tool advertises at least one
property, which would have caught this at the moment it was introduced.

evidence.summary: Reported by two independent playtest leads; confirmed as the only one of 43 tools with no advertised properties.
